why: A path whose ACTION segment is interpolated is a real call to real routes, but
WHICH ones cannot be read from syntax. The matcher refuses to let `<interp>`
satisfy a literal route segment, and that refusal is correct — the alternative
credits `POST /v1/cases/${id}` as a caller of every POST under /v1/cases, which
is exactly the false 'this endpoint is wired' claim the whole exercise exists to
Where the interpolation is a literal-union TYPE the analyzer expands it itself.
What is left is the shape it cannot read: a helper taking `path: string` that
many call sites fill in. Those are answered here, once, from the call sites —
each entry names the file and line whose arguments were read.
The generator refuses an entry whose site no longer exists and an entry naming a
route that is no longer registered, so a refactor cannot leave a stale credit

entries.helper: one toggle whose leg is the inverse of the rule's current state
entries.evidence: AutomationRuleToggle.tsx:66 `const leg = rule.enabled ? "disable" : "enable"` and :71 `apiFetch(`/v1/automation/rules/${encodeURIComponent(rule.id)}/${leg}`, { method: "POST" })`. The path is built from a ternary over two literals, so BOTH legs are reachable from this single control — a rule that is enabled shows Disable and vice versa. The analyzer resolved one branch; this records the other so the pair is not split between PRODUCT_CONNECTED and MISSING_UI when they are the same button. entries.helper: — the browser issues the GET when the element mounts
entries.evidence: The URL is not a literal at the element: the API returns `bytesUrl` per asset and apps/web/lib/media-intelligence/useDerivedAssets.ts:118 normalises it through `normalizeAssetUrls`, which prepends `apiBaseUrl()` to any leading-slash path (useDerivedAssets.ts:32-37) — so the element addresses the API origin, not the Next origin. Both elements set `crossOrigin="use-credentials"` (MediaIntelligencePanel.tsx:285, :362), which is what makes the authenticated bytes route answer 200 rather than 401. The bytes route itself is the server-side proxy that streams from storage (services/api/src/routes/media-intelligence.routes.ts:1276) and never projects a storage key or signed URL. All three facts are pinned by an EXECUTED guard: apps/web/__tests__/phase13-disconnected-ui-actions.test.ts (NEW-028). Recorded as a reviewed resolution because a runtime-valued `src` is not statically resolvable — the analyzer's own JSX resource-element detection covers only literal and constant-resolvable URLs.
